name: Sirikanya Tansakun
role: Deputy Leader of the People's Party, Member of the House of Representatives (Party List)
notes: Chief economic policymaker for Move Forward Party and People's Party. Primary sponsor of the Draft Wealth Tax Act (ร่าง พ.ร.บ. ภาษีความมั่งคั่ง พ.ศ. ....) submitted to the House of Representatives.

name: People's Party
role: Political party
notes: Main opposition party in the House of Representatives, reconstituted in August 2024 following the dissolution of Move Forward Party. Retained all 143 MPs and formally committed to passing the Draft Wealth Tax Act as part of its equality package.

name: Move Forward Party
role: Political party (2020–2024)
notes: Won the 2023 general election with 151 seats. Included an annual net wealth tax of 0.5% over 300M THB in its Progressive Welfare platform and sponsored the Draft Wealth Tax Act in parliament before being dissolved by the Constitutional Court in August 2024.

name: Sustarum Thammaboosadee
role: Associate Professor, College of Interdisciplinary Studies, Thammasat University
notes: Political economist, welfare state scholar, and Board Member of the Social Security Office. Formally proposed a 1% wealth tax on assets over 30 million THB to the We Fair network to fund universal welfare.

name: Ekkaponnat Nattapattanan
role: Assistant Professor, Department of Social Sciences, Faculty of Arts, Silpakorn University
notes: Author of comparative research and monograph analyzing Scandinavian and Swiss net wealth taxes as structural financing mechanisms for a Thai universal welfare state.

name: Duangmanee Laovakul
role: Assistant Professor, Faculty of Economics, Thammasat University
notes: Prominent public finance economist. Formally proposed introducing a net wealth tax (Wealth Tax) and capital gains tax to finance a sustainable national pension fund.

name: Pisit Puapan
role: Director of Macroeconomic Policy Bureau, Fiscal Policy Office (FPO), Ministry of Finance
notes: Senior economist at the Fiscal Policy Office, Ministry of Finance. Advocated expanding Thailand's future revenue base to include a wealth tax base (ฐานภาษีความมั่งคั่ง) to address acute wealth concentration.

name: Decharut Sukkumnoed
role: Director, Think Forward Center
notes: Director of the Think Forward Center think tank. Key designer of progressive tax policy proposals, defending a net wealth tax on assets over 300 million THB to finance public healthcare, education, and universal pensions.

name: We Fair Network
role: Civil society coalition for universal welfare
notes: Major Thai civil society coalition (เครือข่ายรัฐสวัสดิการเพื่อความเท่าเทียมและเป็นธรรม) advocating cradle-to-grave universal welfare funded by wealth taxation and progressive tax reform; drafted a parallel civil society wealth tax bill.

name: Rapeepat Ingkasit
role: Economic journalist, researcher, and author
notes: Economic journalist and author. Published op-ed column on The Matter advocating a 3% annual net wealth tax on top billionaires, coupled with a national wealth registry and exit tax.

name: Thanathorn Juangroongruangkit
role: Chairman of the Progressive Movement, Former Leader of Future Forward Party
notes: Billionaire industrialist (Thai Summit Group), founder of Future Forward Party, and Chairman of the Progressive Movement. On the 2023 campaign trail, explicitly advocated establishing a wealth tax on the rich with net assets exceeding 300 million THB to raise 60 billion THB annually for universal welfare.

name: Supalak Bamrungkit
role: Independent researcher; former policy analyst, labor policy wing of Future Forward/Move Forward
notes: Co-authored a commissioned research project applying net wealth taxation to improve workers' quality of life; the project explicitly recommends a wealth tax to reduce inequality.

name: Nitirat Sapsomboon
role: Director of the We Fair Network
notes: Proposed a wealth tax on the very wealthy to finance universal welfare.

name: Four Regions Slum Network
role: Civil society network
notes: Jointly proposed wealth taxation in an August 2023 letter on universal pensions.

name: People's Network for Welfare State
role: Civil society network
notes: Jointly proposed wealth taxation in an August 2023 letter on universal pensions.

name: Kritsada Theerakosonphong
role: Researcher, Faculty of Social Administration, Thammasat University
notes: Social policy scholar who proposed a wealth tax as an option for financing welfare.

name: Pasuk Phongpaichit
role: Emeritus professor of economics, Chulalongkorn University
notes: Proposed introducing a tax on wealth, including land, to help fund public welfare.

name: Thailand Consumers Council
role: Consumer organisation
notes: Its pension policy proposal cites collecting net wealth tax among options to finance universal pensions.

name: Wiwatchai Atthakor
role: Public administration scholar
notes: Published a recommendation for a wealth tax on Thai billionaires; proposal does not specify a comprehensive tax base.

name: People's Movement for a Just Society (P-Move)
role: Civil society coalition
notes: Coalition includes wealth tax separately from land and capital gains taxes in welfare policy proposals; supersedes exclusion X0008.

name: Theepakorn Jithitikulchai
role: Associate professor of economics
notes: Health and welfare economist whose research presentation recommends wealth taxation of the rich and who discusses its benefits in a 2023 article.

name: Labour Network for People's Rights
role: Coalition of labour organisations
notes: Coalition of organised labour groups; its 2021 open letter called for a wealth tax on the richest 1% to fund universal welfare.
